counting: One formal workflow incident; multiple GPU exceptions and diagnostic reproductions not counted again. Includes historical prerequisite profile OOMs even if later repaired. Excludes predicted OOM/no-feasible.
fragmentation_rule: Possible only when visible device free + PyTorch reserved-unallocated >= requested allocation. This is a heuristic, not proof that cache is releasable or fragmentation caused failure.

incidents.assessment: Visible free plus all unallocated cache still insufficient; capacity shortage evidenced
incidents.raw_exception: torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 37.09 GiB. GPU 5 has a total capacity of 95.07 GiB of which 29.06 GiB is free. Including non-PyTorch memory, this process has 66.00 GiB memory in use. Of the allocated memory 63.33 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, and 237.41 MiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. If reserved but unallocated memory is large try setting PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True to avoid fragmentation.  See documentation for Memory Management  (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda.html#environment-variables)

primary_reporting_scope: Actual CUDA OOM in selected-configuration formal training only. Profile-stage OOM is auxiliary workflow reliability data; predicted infeasibility is separate.
attribution_policy: Same workload completing with only allocator settings changed is recorded as memory management sensitive, with original OOM retained; this is not evidence of intrinsic capacity prediction failure or proof of overall prediction accuracy.
